//: The pages the harness draws into references/books/, each through the client's own book screen as a written book of that one page is read: the book's background, then the page's text, which the screen wraps at 114 GUI pixels and draws in the page's black from its own origin, at most fourteen lines, with the page-number line left out by the screen's own flag. A subject naming no page is the background alone, the one drawing every page shares; empty draws the whole step over an empty page, and the same pixels. Every colour and format is spelled as a JSON field except on section_codes and reset_across_break, whose text holds section-sign codes, each sign and the character after it a format code to the client. section_codes holds no reset. reset_across_break holds the resets the client's wrap and its draw read differently: the wrap reads a reset as no style and opens the line after a break in the style in force there, which after a reset is no style and the screen draws white with a shadow, while the draw returns a reset to the style its line opens in. No page is obfuscated: the client's obfuscation random is unseeded, so such a page would not reproduce. Translatable components are out, resolving through the client's language; selector, score and NBT components are out, being resolved by a server in play; hover and click events draw nothing on a still page nobody points at; private-use glyphs are out. Every page is drawn over vanilla's own resources alone, and every key is lowercase, as every reference stem is.
